newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI panel for easier share transfer norms.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI panel for easier share transfer norms.

text.p: Indian companies and state-run firms should delegate powers to speed up share transfers, a panel set up by the market regulator said on Wednesday.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said share transfer agents must be empowered to approve share transfers. Presently, share transfers are approved only by a company's board of directors.
"The power should include the authority to sign as authorised signatory of the endorsement of transfer," the SEBI said in a statement.
Stockbrokers must be asked to attest signatures of sellers in a share certificate, the panel said, adding that the brokers should also be liable to make good any losses due to fraud.

"The primary intent of these measures is to bring about a radical and paradigm shift in the share transfer process with the ultimate objective of improving investor confidence and foster healthy development of the capital market," it said.
Share transfer agents will be required to return transferred certificates within 10 days of lodgement. It will also eliminate rejections of transfers due to signature differences, the SEBI said.
Currently, share transfers take about three months from the point of sale.
